text: She walked out of Carnegie's mansion... and dropped a two-million-dollar note he never signed.
A man from Ohio saw it... and one day, an Ohio bank would collapse.
Her secret, she told him: she was Carnegie's daughter.
Soon banks were lending to Carnegie's "daughter." Nobody asked Carnegie.
Some at twenty-five percent. By one estimate, about two million dollars in all.
She played the heiress on Cleveland's Euclid Avenue.
Then one lender wanted his hundred and ninety thousand back.
Carnegie's office said: he didn't know her, and hadn't signed a note in over thirty years.
In Oberlin, Ohio, depositors ran on their bank. It failed.
She died in prison three years later.
Carnegie never gave her a cent. The banks did... for his name.
